guard: cotal_inbox clears only the messages it actually returned, and one response stays inside a receivable window with first-party mail ahead of replayed history
why: The defect this guards is a composition, so the kills are split along the three parts of it
rather than aimed at one line. K1 removes the window (payload-exceeds-receivable), K2 restores
the old drain-the-whole-scope order (destructive read), K3 removes mail-before-replay (the
reason a DM survives the first window at all), K4 lets peek clear, and K5 silences the note
that tells a caller the rest is still there.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, checked rather than assumed. The suite imports the agent and the tool specs
by RELATIVE SOURCE PATH (../src/agent.js, ../src/tool-specs.js), so the bytes mutated are the
bytes graded: no dist in the path and no build in the command. Its only package-name import is
`type` from @cotal-ai/core, erased at compile time and carrying no behaviour.
NOT PROVED HERE, named rather than implied. The 48,000-character budget is a judgement, not a
measurement of any one host's cap: no mutation can show it is the RIGHT number, only that a
bound is enforced and that what falls outside it is kept. And the oversized-single-item escape
(one message larger than the whole budget is shown alone) is asserted by no cell, because the
measured occupant has no such message; it is stated in the source instead.

mutations.name: K1 the window selects everything — the response is capped by nothing
mutations.replace: if (false && shown.length && used + cost > budget) held.push(i);
mutations.expectRed: the response is inside the receivable window, not 463,788 chars
mutations.cell: the response is inside the receivable window, not 463,788 chars
mutations.note: This is the pre-fix behaviour exactly: everything selected, one response, 463,788 chars on the measured occupant.

mutations.name: K2 clear the whole scope up front, the order the defect was written in
mutations.expectRed: what did not fit was NOT consumed: the buffer still holds the rest
mutations.cell: what did not fit was NOT consumed: the buffer still holds the rest
mutations.note: The plausible authoring error rather than a contrived one: draining the scope is what the tool did before, and with a window in place it reads as a harmless simplification.

mutations.name: K3 rank every item the same — receive order alone decides the window
mutations.expectRed: the first response is mail, not backfill: DMs occupy the window ahead of replayed history
mutations.cell: the first response is mail, not backfill: DMs occupy the window ahead of replayed history
mutations.note: Without the rank a DM behind a replay waits for as many calls as the replay takes; the loss is gone but the mail is still last.

mutations.name: K4 peek clears what it shows
mutations.note: peek is the documented workaround for this very defect, so a peek that clears is the worst possible regression here.

mutations.name: K5 the response stops saying what it is holding back
mutations.expectRed: ...and it says what it is holding back
mutations.cell: ...and it says what it is holding back
mutations.note: Held mail nobody is told about is mail nobody calls back for — the loss becomes a silent delay instead.
